images.title: Two number lines that stretch together
images.purpose: Shows the double number line in its simplest state: 500 mL fills in 15 seconds, so 10000 mL fills in 300 seconds.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two long parallel horizontal number lines across the middle, starting at the same left point, with one factor arrow for each line.
images.exact_structure: Top line in teal (#0072B2), titled mL at its left end; bottom line in amber (#E69F00), titled seconds at its left end. Both lines start at the same left point with an unlabelled tick. On each line exactly two labelled ticks, vertically aligned between the lines: on the top line 500 near the left (one twentieth of the way) and 10000 near the right end; on the bottom line 15 under 500 and 300 under 10000. Exactly two curved reddish purple (#CC79A7) arrows: one above the top line from 500 to 10000 and one below the bottom line from 15 to 300, each labelled × 20. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Proportional quantities stretch by the same factor: 500 mL to 10000 mL is × 20, so 15 s becomes 300 s.
images.description: Shows the double number line in its simplest state: 500 mL fills in 15 seconds, so 10000 mL fills in 300 seconds.
images.context: 10 litres is 10000 mL; 10000 ÷ 500 = 20; 15 × 20 = 300 seconds, which is 5 minutes.

image_decisions.why: The tool's core view, two aligned lines and one factor, in its plainest state.
